rows.speaker: الشافعى
rows.claim: Al-Shafi'i, as reported by al-Wahidi, treats Quran as a proper, non-derived name for God's Book.
rows.anchor: قال الواحدى قول الشافعى هو اسم لكتاب الله يعنى أنه اسم علم غير مشتق

rows.speaker: الأشعرى
rows.claim: Al-Ash'ari derives Quran from joining: it brings together its suras, verses, and letters, like qiran joins pilgrimage rites.
rows.anchor: مشتق من قرنت الشىء بالشىء إذا ضممته إليه فسمى بذلك لقرآن السور والآيات والحروف فيه ومنه قيل للجمع بين الحج والعمرة قران قال وإلى هذا المعنى ذهب الأشعرى

rows.speaker: القرطبى
rows.claim: Al-Qurtubi derives the unhamzated form from qarā'in because Quranic verses confirm and resemble one another.
rows.anchor: قال القرطبى القران بغير همز مأخوذ من القرائن لأن الآيات منه يصدق بعضها بعضا ويشابه بعضها بعضا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj rejects al-Qurtubi's derivation: the unhamzated pronunciation reflects ease, transferring the hamza vowel to the preceding consonant; al-Farisi noted this analysis.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وهذا القول سهو والصحيح أن ترك الهمز فيه من باب التخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers the Quran in the Prophet's heart as memorization, on his tongue as recitation, and in his hearing as understanding and knowledge.
rows.anchor: أى جمعه فى قلبك حفظا وعلى لسانك تلاوة وفى سمعك فهما وعلما

rows.speaker: بعض أصحابنا
rows.claim: Some of the author's colleagues say the listener hears a created recitation while understanding through it God's eternal speech.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أصحابنا إن عند قراءة القارىء تسمع قراءته المخلوقة ويفهم منها كلام الله القديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, being told not to hear the Quran means not to understand or reason about it; physical hearing occurs whether a listener wills it or not.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى قوله ﴿ لا تسمعوا لهذا القرآن ﴾ أى لا تفهموا ولا تعقلوا لأن السمع الطبيعي يحصل للسامع شاء أو أبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kalam is linked to impact: speech is called kalam because it impresses on the listener's mind a benefit previously unknown to them.
rows.anchor: وأما الكلام فمشتق من التأثير يقال كلمة إذا أثر فيه بالجرح فسمى الكلام كلاما لأنه يؤثر فى ذهن السامع فائدة لم تكن عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is called light because it lets people discern subtle matters of the lawful and unlawful.
rows.anchor: وأما النور فلأنه يدرك به غوامض الحلال والحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called guidance because it clearly points to truth and distinguishes truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته هدى فلأن فيه دلالة بينة إلى الحق وتفريقا بينه وبين الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called remembrance for its exhortations, warnings, and accounts of past nations; dhikr is the verbal noun of remembering.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته ذكرا فلما فيه من المواعظ والتحذير وأخبار الأمم الماضية وهو مصدر ذكرت ذكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikr can also mean honor: the cited verse says the Book contains the people's renown.
rows.anchor: قال تعالى ﴿ لقد أنزلنا إليكم كتابا فيه ذكركم ﴾ أى شرفكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called clarification because it explains the kinds of truth and lays out their proofs.
rows.anchor: أما تسميته تبيانا فلأنه بين فيه أنواع الحق وكشف أدلته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called a message because the Prophet's reports and delivery reached people through it.
rows.anchor: أما تسميته بلاغا فلأنه لم يصل إليهم حال أخبار النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم وإبلاغه إليهم إلا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called manifest because it makes clear and separates truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته مبينا فلأنه أبان وفرق بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called bringer of glad tidings and warner because it promises Paradise and warns of the Fire.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته بشيرا ونذيرا فلأنه بشر بالجنة وأنذر من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aziz means that imitators cannot produce the Quran's like; the challenge concerns its reports and recitation in their striking composition, since eternal speech has no counterpart.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته عزيزا أى يعجز ويعز على من يروم أن يأتى بمثله فيتعذر ذلك عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation of aziz is that a reciter who acts by the Quran is not humiliated.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالعزيز نفى المهانة عن قارئه إذا عمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called Furqan because it distinguishes truth from falsehood and believers from unbelievers, including believers from hypocrites; this also explains Umar's title al-Faruq.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته فرقانا فلأنه فرق بين الحق والباطل والمسلم والكافر والمؤمن والمنافق وبه سمى عمر بن الخطاب الفارق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation of mathani is that the Quran's accounts of earlier scriptures provide a second exposition that clarifies the earlier account.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته مثانى فلأن فيه بيان قصص الكتب الماضية فيكون البيان ثانيا للأول الذى تقدمه فيبين الأول الثانى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view derives mathani from the repeated rulings, stories, and exhortations in the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقيل سمى مثانى لتكرار الحكم والقصص والمواعظ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view takes mathani as the name of al-Fatiha alone.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه اسم الفاتحة وحدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahy means communicating something secretly, whether by speech to prophets or angels, inspiration to bees, or ants' signs; the term also connotes swift, hidden inspiration.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته وحيا ومعناه تعريف الشىء خفية سواء كان بالكلام كالأنبياء والملائكة أو بإلهام كالنحل وإشارة النمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called wise because its verses establish lawful and unlawful rulings and defy imitation; learning and practicing it restrains indecency.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته حكيما فلأن آياته أحكمت بذكر الحلال والحرام فأحكمت عن الإتيان بمثلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called confirming because it affirms earlier prophets or their scriptures before alteration.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته مصدقا فإنه صدق الأنبياء الماضين أو كتبهم قبل أن تغير وتبدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called a guardian because it testifies that earlier scriptures came from God.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته مهيمنا فلأنه الشاهد للكتب المتقدمة بأنها من عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name balagh reflects its role in informing people, conveying the message, and delivering it.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته بلاغا فلأنه كان فى الإعلام والإبلاغ وأداء الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called healing because faith cures unbelief and learning with practice cures ignorance.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته شفاء فلأنه من آمن به كان له شفاء من سقم الكفر ومن علمه وعمل به كان له شفاء من سقم الجهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called mercy because understanding and comprehending it bring mercy to the person.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته رحمة فإن من فهمه وعقله كان رحمة له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called stories because it recounts the reports and histories of earlier nations.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته قصصا فلأن فيه قصص الأمم الماضين وأخبارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majid means noble; part of the Quran's nobility is its preservation from alteration, addition, and subtraction.
rows.anchor: وأم تسميته مجيدا والمجيد الشريف فمن شرفه أنه حفظ عن التغيير والتبديل والزيادة والنقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is itself miraculous in that no one can produce its like.
rows.anchor: وجعله معجزا فى نفسه عن أن يؤتى بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanzil is the verbal noun of revelation: God made Gabriel hear and understand His speech as He willed, without description or modality, and Gabriel conveyed it to the Prophet as learned.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته تنزيلا فلأنه مصدر نزلته لأنه منزل من عند الله على لسان جبريل لأن الله تعالى أسمع جبريل كلامه وفهمه إياه كما شاء من غير وصف ولا كيفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basair derives from sight and insight and encompasses the aims of believers, as the Quran says it includes the moist and the dry.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته بصائر فلأنه مشتق من البصر والبصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhikra reminds believers of the oneness of God on which He created them.
rows.anchor: وأما تسميته ذكرى فلأنه ذكر للمؤمنين ما فطرهم الله عليه من التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited verse, al-Zabur means all revealed books, not only David's Psalms; al-dhikr means the Mother of the Book from God.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بالزبور هنا جميع الكتب المنزلة من السماء لا يختص بزبور داود والذكر أم الكتاب الذى من عند الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu means possessor or owner, as in the phrases about the Throne and the two gardens; it is used in a construct and does not take an adjective or personal pronoun as its complement.
rows.anchor: بمعنى صاحب ومنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu lets Arabic describe individuals by a generic quality: a bare abstract quality does not specialize a person, while dhu knowledge does; the adjective then follows its noun in case and meaning.
rows.anchor: وانما وضعت وصلة إلى وصف الاشخاص بالاجناس كما إن الذي وضعت وصلة إلى وصل المعارف بالجمل

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's reading, above every possessor of a learned one is a more learned one, has the same meaning as the canonical possessor of knowledge reading.
rows.anchor: واما قراءة ابن مسعود / وفوق كل ذي عالم عليم /

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical analysis treats dhu as redundant in the phrase.
rows.anchor: وقيل ذي زائد ة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis reads the construction as annexing the named quality to its referent: a person named or described as learned.
rows.anchor: وقيل من اضافة المسمى إلا الاسم اي وفوق كل ذي شخص يسمى عالما أو يقال له عالم عليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu cannot be annexed to a personal pronoun; the author calls the expression dhuwayhi in a prayer for Muhammad ungrammatical.
rows.anchor: ولا يضاف إلى ضمير الاشخاص ولهذا لحنوا قول بعضهم صلى الله على محمد وذويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most grammarians bar dhu from annexation to a generic pronoun, but the author considers it apparently permissible because a generic pronoun means the genus itself.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا هل تضاف ذو إلى ضمير الاجناس فمنعه الاكثرون والظاهر الجواز لان ضمير الجنس هو الجنس في المعنى

rows.speaker: ابن بري
rows.claim: Ibn Barri says dhu parallels sahib and may be annexed wherever sahib can; only its connective use bars attachment to a pronoun.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن بري انها تضاف إلى ما يضاف إليه صاحب لانها رديفته وانه لايمتنع اضافتها للضمير إلا اذا كانت وصلة

rows.speaker: المطرزي
rows.claim: Al-Mutarrizi says dhu, meaning companion or possessor, requires a described noun and a complement; he gives forms for masculine, feminine, dual, and plural, including a fetus and what a hen lays.
rows.anchor: وقال المطرزي ( 1 ) في المغرب ذو بمعنى الصاحب تقتضي شيئين موصوفا ومضافا إليه

rows.speaker: المطرزي
rows.claim: Al-Mutarrizi explains that the word later became an independent noun, producing expressions such as an individuated essence, an eternal or originated essence, and essential attributes.
rows.anchor: ثم اقتطعوا عنها مقتضاها واجروها مجرى الاسماء التامة المستقلة غير المقتضية لما سواها فقالوا ذات متميزة وذات قديمة ومحدثة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the verse combines three parables: as foam vanishes as useless scum, falsehood likewise disappears from its adherents.
rows.anchor: روى ابن أبى حاتم عن قتادة قال هذه ثلاثة أمثال ضربها الله فى مثل واحد يقول كما اضمحل هذا الزبد فصار جفاء لا ينتفع به

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A sound prophetic report compares revealed guidance and knowledge to rain received differently by soils: some yield growth, some store water for people, and some barren ground retains or produces nothing; these represent people who benefit, preserve, or reject guidance.
rows.anchor: وفى الحديث الصحيح إن مثل ما بعثنى الله به من الهدى والعلم كمثل غيث أصاب أرضا فكان منها طائفة قبلت الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives hypocrites two parables, one of fire and one of rain.
rows.anchor: وقد ضرب الله للمنافقين مثلين مثلا بالنار ومثلا بالمطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb aḍāʾa is transitive in the fire parable because the fire illuminates its surroundings, but intransitive for lightning, which shines on its own and may not light the people nearby.
rows.anchor: يقال أضاء الشىء وأضاءه غيره فيستعمل لازما متعديا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire parable says God took away the hypocrites' light rather than saying it went out, since its heat could remain and harm them.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل انطفأت بل قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable implies that hypocrites once had light and then lost it, as the Quran says they believed and then disbelieved.
rows.anchor: وهذا المثل يقتضى أن المنافق حصل له نور ثم ذهب كما قال الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author lists Qur'anic legal studies by school: al-Shafi'i first; al-Kiya al-Harrasi among Shafi'is; al-Razi among Hanafis; named Maliki scholars; and Qadi Abu Ya'la among Hanbalis.
rows.anchor: وقد اعتنى بذلك الأئمة وأفردوه وأولهم الشافعي ثم تلاه من أصحابنا ألكيا الهراسي

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari reports that after heavy losses among Quran reciters at Yamama, Umar warned Abu Bakr that more deaths could cause Quranic material to be lost and urged its collection; Abu Bakr hesitated because the Prophet had not done so, but Umar persuaded him.
rows.anchor: روى البخارى فى صحيحه عن زيد بن ثابت قال أرسل إلى أبو بكر مقتل أهل اليمامة فإذا عمر بن الخطاب عنده

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Abu Bakr chose Zayd, a young, trusted writer of revelation, to gather the Quran; after initial hesitation, Zayd collected it from writing materials and people's memories.
rows.anchor: إنك رجل شاب عاقل لا أتهمك وقد كنت تكتب الوحى لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فتتبع القرآن واجمعه قال زيد فوالله لوكلفنى نقل جبل

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: Zayd says he found the last verse of al-Tawba only with Abu Khuzayma al-Ansari, whose testimony the Prophet counted as two, and inserted it in its sura; the sheets passed from Abu Bakr to Umar to Hafsa.
rows.anchor: حتى وجدت آخر التوبة

rows.speaker: زيد بن ثابت
rows.claim: In a report through Ibn Shihab and Kharija, Zayd says he remembered a verse of al-Ahzab heard from the Prophet but found its written witness only with Khuzayma; it was added to the sura, and Khuzayma's testimony counted as two.
rows.anchor: وفى رواية ابن شهاب وأخبرنى خارجة بن زيد سمع زيد بن ثابت يقول فقدت آية من الأحزاب حين نسخنا المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd's search for corroboration does not mean the Quran was established by one person's report: Zayd already knew the verses and their placements from the Prophet, and sought witnesses for reassurance after others had forgotten them.
rows.anchor: ليس فيه إثبات القرآن بخبر الواحد لأن زيدا كان قد سمعها وعلم موضعها فى سورة الأحزاب بتعليم النبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four Companions known as Quran preservers were renowned examples, not the only memorizers; the whole Quran was memorized and arranged during the Prophet's life, apart from the cited exception of Bara'a.
rows.anchor: والمراد أن هؤلاء كانوا اشتهروا به فقد ثبت أن غيرهم حفظه وثبت أن القرآن مجموعة محفوظ كله صدور الرجال أيام حياة النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context can resolve ambiguity, rule out unintended readings, specify general wording, and restrict unqualified wording; ignoring it leads to error. Thus the address 'the mighty, noble one' in context means the truly lowly and contemptible.
rows.anchor: الرابع دلالة السياق فإنها ترشد إلى تبيين المجمل والقطع بعدم احتمال غير المراد وتخصيص العام وتقييد المطلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A word can pass through successive metaphoric extensions until its original rationale is obscure; dun first means a lower place, then inferiority, rank, and finally crossing a boundary or ruling.
rows.anchor: اصل دون للمكان الذي هو أنزل من مكان غيره ومنه الشيء الدون للحقير ثم استعير للتفاوت في الأحوال والرتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus the prohibition on taking unbelievers as allies min dun the believers means not to pass from the alliance of believers to that of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والتقدير لا تتجاوزوا ولاية المؤمنين إلى ولاية الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If min dun God modifies invoke, the challenge means to go beyond God and invoke the idols claimed to testify for the challengers on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: أي تجاوزوا الله في دعائكم إلى دعاء آلهتكم الذين تزعمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If min dun God modifies invoke, another reading is that one should not invoke God as a witness, since that is an appeal for the litigant without proof to rely on; instead bring evidence accepted by judges.
rows.anchor: أي لاتستشهدوا بالله فإنها حجة يركن إليها العاجز عن البينات من الناس بل ائتوا ببينة تكون حجة عند الحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If min dun God modifies your witnesses, it can mean the alleged witnesses who supposedly bypass God's testimony for you at the Resurrection, or the idols whose divinity you chose over God's.
rows.anchor: احتمل معنيين أحدهما أن يكون المعنى ادعوا الذين تجاوزتم في زعمكم شهادة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further construction takes the witnesses as people other than believers who will testify that the challengers believe in a comparable revelation.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون التقدير من دون الله أي من غير المؤمنين يشهدون لكم أنكم آمنتم بمثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This reading lets the challengers rely on the fact that eloquent speakers would disdain answering clear truth with incoherent falsehood.
rows.anchor: وهذا يؤذن بأنه لم يبق تشبث سوى قولهم الله يشهد لنا عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording needs no extra emphasis because it explicitly says they might be the first to cast; this is a rhetorical, not syntactic, answer.
rows.anchor: انما لم يؤكد في الاية لانه استغنى عن التاكيد بالتصريح بالاولية

words: إِمَّآ أَن تَلْقِىَ وَإِمَّآ أَن نَّكُونَ
rows.speaker: ابن جنى
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the longer wording as matching the sura's verse endings and conveying the sorcerers' confidence and hauteur toward Moses; assigning the act to him gives their words fuller force.
rows.anchor: احدهما لفظي وهو المزاوجه لرءوس الآي على سياق خواتمها من اول السورة إلى آخرها

rows.speaker: ابن جنى
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says dialogue attributed to people from earlier nations preserves their recognizable meanings, not necessarily their exact words; the polished Arabic speech attributed to non-Arabs is therefore no objection.
rows.anchor: ذكر ذلك ابن جني في خاطرياته ثم اورد سؤالا وهو انا نعلم ان السحرة لم يكونوا اهل لسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beginning a clause with a subject pronoun adds emphasis and, according to some, exclusivity.
rows.anchor: التاسع تصدير الجملة بضمير مبتدأ يفيد التأكيد ولهذا قيل بافادة الحصر

rows.speaker: الزمخشرى
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari reads the pronoun as exclusive: only these people believe in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: قال في قوله تعالى ﴿ وبالآخرة هم يوقنون ﴾ معناه الحصر

rows.speaker: الزمخشرى
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari likewise says the pronoun means only the alleged earthly gods can resurrect, exposing the polytheists' implication that divinity is exclusive to them.
rows.anchor: وقال في قوله ﴿ أم اتخذوا آلهة من الأرض هم ينشرون ﴾ ان معناه لاينشر الا هم

rows.speaker: الزمخشرى
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari departs from his exclusivity rule in this verse, reading the pronoun as intensifying the force of the statement rather than restricting it, which the author attributes to his doctrine.
rows.anchor: ثم خالف هذه القاعدة لما خالف مذهبه الفاسد في قوله تعالى ﴿ وما هم بخارجين من النار ﴾ فقال هم هنا بمنزلتها

rows.speaker: ابن بابشاذ
rows.claim: Ibn Babshadh limits the preceding point to cases where the two people face the qibla; the excerpt does not restate what that point concerns.
rows.anchor: قال ابن بابشاذ وإنما يصح هذا إذا كانا متوجهين نحو القبلة

rows.speaker: السهيلى
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli notes that right-hand plural forms usually denote few, whereas left-hand shama'il is a plural of abundance; an intensive context favors a form signaling abundance.
rows.anchor: إن اليمين يجمع على أيمن وأيمان فهو من أبنية جمع القلة غالبا والشمال يجمع على شمائل وهو جمع كثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-shimal remains singular for the people of that direction because their destination is one: the infernal abode on the left.
rows.anchor: وأما إفرادها في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Right and left are singular because each person has one recorder on each side, recording good and evil.
rows.anchor: فإن لكل عبد قعيدا واحدا عن يمينه وآخر شماله يحصيان عليه الخير والشر فلا معنى للجمع بينهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan's sides are plural because he seeks to mislead many; the paired clauses distribute multiple sides across multiple targets.
rows.anchor: فإن الجمع هناك يقابله كثير مما يريد إغوائهم فجمع لمقابلة الجملة بالجملة المقتضي لتوزيع الأفراد على الأفراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens may be named in singular or plural because they differ in kind, while Fire is singular as one genus.
rows.anchor: لما كانت الجنات مختلفة الأنواع حسن جمعها وإفرادها ولما كانت النار واحدة أفردت باعتبار الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular cup in the cited verse illustrates the singular form used for a unified kind, rather than a plural of cups.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل وكؤوس لما سنذكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation pairs plural Paradise with mercy and singular Fire with punishment, as wind is plural in mercy and singular in punishment.
rows.anchor: أنه لما كانت النار تعذيبا والجنة رحمة ناسب جمع الرحمة وإفراد العذاب نظير جمع الريح في الرحمة وإفرادها في العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation likens Fire to a prison where many prisoners are crowded, while a generous host gives each enduring guest a prepared home; Paradise is plural, Fire singular.
rows.anchor: فالنار دار حبس والغاضب يجمع جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Plural verses indicate multiple proofs, while a singular sign reflects the oneness of what is being demonstrated.
rows.anchor: فحيث جمعت فلجمع الدلائل وحيث وحدت فلوحدانية المدلول عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural in the verse for those who discern contrasts with the singular sign for believers, whose quality is described by divine oneness.
rows.anchor: فلما ذكر صفة المؤمنين بالوحدانية وحد الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular sign in this verse is a parallel to the singular sign for believers in al-Hijr.
rows.anchor: وليس لها نظير إلا في العنكبوت وهو قوله

words: فَلَعَلَّكَ تَارِكٌ بَعْضَ مَا يُوحَىٰ إِلَيْكَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La'alla can report what people suppose about someone; in exhortations such as hoping for success, it denotes expectation, as in the cited hope for God's mercy.
rows.anchor: اي تظن بك الناس وعليه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some restrict la'alla to possible outcomes because expectation concerns the possible; Pharaoh's apparent hope of reaching God reflects his ignorance and belief that God occupies a body and place.
rows.anchor: وزعم بعضهم بانها لا تكون للترجي إلا في الممكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: La'alla can mean in order that; Tha'lab also takes the phrase about Moses speaking gently so Pharaoh may remember causally.
rows.anchor: الثاني للتعليل كقوله تعالى ﴿ فاتبعوه واتقوا لعلكم ترحمون ﴾

words: لَعَلَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحْدِثُ بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ أَمْرًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third use of la'alla is interrogative, as in the warning that one cannot know whether God will bring about a later matter.
rows.anchor: الثالث الاستفهام كقوله تعالى ﴿ لا تدري لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا ﴾

rows.speaker: الواقدى
rows.claim: Al-Waqidi, as quoted by al-Baghawi, says every Quranic la'alla is causal except here, where it means as if; the author calls this simile reading unusual among grammarians.
rows.anchor: وحكى البغوي في تفسيره عن الواقدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Bukhari also gives la'alla here a simile meaning, while another view takes it as straightforward hope relative to the people addressed.
rows.anchor: ووقع في صحيح البخاري في قوله ﴿ لعلكم تخلدون ﴾ إن لعل للتشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expectation and wishing are performative constructions, raising the question of how they can govern past-tense content; the Quran uses a past verb after la-yta.
rows.anchor: واعلم أن الترجي والتمني من باب الانشاء كيف يتعلقان بالماضي

rows.speaker: الرمانى
rows.claim: Al-Rummani says a past-tense clause cannot serve as the predicate after la'alla.
rows.anchor: وممن نص على منع وقوع الماضي خبرا للعل الرماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most grammarians say laysa negates a clause in the present and does not take a future predicate; other views make its negation general or unrestricted, and Ibn al-Hajib favors the unrestricted view.
rows.anchor: ليس فعل معناه نفي مضمون الجملة في الحال اذا قلت ليس زيدا قائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the present-only analysis because this verse negates that punishment will be turned away in the future; the broader analyses also permit the phrase laysa illa Allah without figurative explanation.
rows.anchor: ورد الاول بقوله ﴿ ألا يوم يأتيهم ليس مصروفا عنهم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expressions God and His Messenger dislike and disliked by your Lord usually indicate prohibition, though they can also mean disfavored but not forbidden.
rows.anchor: وأما لفظ ( يكرهه الله ورسوله )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formula As for me, I do not do it signals dislike, as in the Prophet's statement that he does not eat reclining.
rows.anchor: وأما لفظ ( أما أنا فلا أفعل ) فالمحقق فيه الكراهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formulas it is not for you or for us consistently express prohibition in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: وأما لفظ ( ما يكون لك ) و ( ما يكون لنا )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permissibility can be inferred from explicit allowance, removal of blame, permission, pardon, conditional choice, mention of benefits, silence about prohibition, or approval of conduct during revelation.
rows.anchor: وتستفاد الإباحة من لفظ الإحلال ورفع الجناح والإذن والعفو

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir's report that the Companions practiced withdrawal while the Quran was being revealed exemplifies divine tacit approval; Hasan's poetry recitation before the Prophet exemplifies prophetic approval when aware.
rows.anchor: فمن إقرار الرب قول جابر ( كنا نعزل والقرآن ينزل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse about adornment, eating, drinking, and avoiding excess gathers the foundations of legal address: command, prohibition, permission, and choice.
rows.anchor: جمعت أصول أحكام الشريعة كلها فجمعت الأمر والنهي والإباحة والتخيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine rebuke preceding an act indicates its prohibition; the author cites five rebukes across al-Anfal, al-Tawba, al-Ahzab, al-Tahrim, and Abasa, contrasting Ibn Abd al-Salam's treatment of rebuke as evidence for a prohibition.
rows.anchor: تقديم العتاب على الفعل من الله تعالى يدل على تحريمه فقد عاتب الله سبحانه في خمسة مواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One cannot claim divine favor for something forbidden; the author rejects the view that the favor is creation of an ability to endure it.
rows.anchor: لا يصح الإمتنان بممنوع عنه خلافا لمن زعم أنه يصح ويصرف الإمتنان إلى خلقه للصبر عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Expressions of divine wonder can signal approval, as in reports about a youth without youthful vice or a man rising for prayer, or disapproval, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: فقد يدل على بغض الفعل

rows.speaker: السهيلى
rows.claim: Al-Suhayli says the feminine marker is omitted where the cry means punishment and disgrace, linked to the phrase about disgrace that day, strengthening masculine agreement; that link is absent in Shuayb's story.
rows.anchor: وأبدى السهيلي للحذف والإثبات معنى حسنا فقال إنما حذفت منه لأن الصيحة فيها بمعنى العذاب والخزي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation treats al-sayha as the verbal noun meaning shouting, which permits masculine agreement; when it means one occurrence of the event, feminine agreement is better.
rows.anchor: وأجاب غيره بأن الصيحة يراد بها المصدر بمعنى الصياح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shuayb's people faced three punishments: quake, scorching heat, then a cloud where they sought shade before the cry struck; naming the cry as a feminine event fits the sequence.
rows.anchor: وقد أخبر سبحانه عن العذاب الذي أصاب به قوم شعيب بثلاثة أمور كلها مفردة اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Compared with the phrase about a group on whom misguidance was decreed, the greater separation between verb and subject in the other wording better licenses omission of feminine agreement.
rows.anchor: أما اللفظي فهو أن الفصل بين الفعل والفاعل في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this verse, min refers back to the feminine noun community, so feminine agreement in haqqat is fitting; the next phrase has the same meaning, but the feminine marker echoes the referent.
rows.anchor: وأما المعنوى فهو أن من في قوله

words: فَرِيقًا هَدَىٰ وَفَرِيقًا حَقَّ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلضَّلَٰلَةُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subject team is masculine, so the verb and phrase about misguidance take masculine agreement without the feminine marker.
rows.anchor: فالفريق مذكر ولو قال ضلوا لكان بغير تاء
